cr_data.provenance: Artist; purchased by Caroline Marmon Fesler [1878-1960], Indianapolis, Indiana; given to the John Herron Art Institute, now the Indianapolis Museum of Art at Newfields, in 1943 (43.37). (Source: Indianapolis Museum of Art website, 2025)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "O'Keeffe told me this was in the O'Keeffe exh. at An Amer. Place, No. 13, 'The Black Place No. 2' and painted 1941." Whitney Archive and Downtown Gallery Archive date 1942. Abiquiú Notebooks dates "1942 (possible 1941)." Dated 1941 on basis of a letter from O'Keeffe to Caroline Fesler, which refers to a painting trip in late November 1941 to the area she called the Black Place (about 150 miles west of Abiquiú): "By now you have the Grey Hills.... It is a painting ... of a place that I love. It was the last week of November. We packed up after supper because it was a wonderful night and drove over there in the moonlight .... In the morning I painted." No such trip was made in November 1942. And as she wrote in 1943: "Sold another painting this noon to go to the Indianapolis Museum—It is that largest Black Place from a year ago last fall—pleases me" (O'Keeffe to Maria Chabot, March 1943). (Source: Lynes, 1999)
